description: Adds two more shifted reflect-padded views ([0:32, 2:34] and [2:34, 0:32] slices) to the uncertain-image TTA in _get_tta_logits, so each uncertain test image is averaged over five shifts with flips instead of three.

Adds two more shifted reflect-padded views ([0:32, 2:34] and [2:34, 0:32] slices) to the uncertain-image TTA in _get_tta_logits, so each uncertain test image is averaged over five shifts with flips instead of three.

Adds a residual skip inside each ConvGroup by saving the pooled conv1 output (x_pool, before norm1) and adding it to the conv2 branch after norm2 and before the final SiLU, so the skip always matches shape.

The NaN/inf logits most likely come from BatchNorm's eps=1e-12, which underflows to zero in half precision, so near-zero variance channels divide by zero; raising eps to 1e-5 (representable in fp16) removes that failure mode with a one-line change.
Raise BATCH_SIZE from 1536 to 2048 and scale BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(2048/1536) (about 1.1547) to test the batch-size speed-accuracy tradeoff.
Disable the brightness and contrast jitter by setting the color_jitter enabled flag to False in train()'s aug dict, leaving only flip and translate augmentation.
Reduce the middle block width in CifarNet from 256 to 192 (block1=64, block2=192, block3=256) to cut the dominant 16x16-resolution FLOPs and test the time-accuracy tradeoff along the width axis.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. Nothing is carried from one run to the next or done in the untimed first call. There is no seeding, no use of test images and no file access. The diff only moves the head weight from Nesterov SGD to a third Muon optimizer.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The run is a valid measurement of a worse variant. Its adjusted value of 4.676 is a large rise in cost, which roughly matches an accuracy loss of about 6 points.

Likely cause of the regression: head_lr is tuned for SGD on an unnormalised head. Muon orthogonalises and normalises the update, so reusing head_lr with Muon gives a step of a very different size. The candidate also changes weight decay: it passes wd instead of wd/head_lr. The head now follows the bias schedule (lr_factor2) rather than Muon's schedule.
Changing `len(p.shape) == 4` to `in (2, 4)` also applies to optimizer2. This is harmless only because optimizer2 holds just the 4D conv filters.
No claims accompany the diff, so there is nothing to check against the numbers. Reject is the right decision.

z cannot be recomputed exactly because the harness's sd is not given. Assuming a job sd of 0.026 and 15 incumbent runs, the standard error is 0.026*sqrt(1+1/15) ≈ 0.0269, so z ≈ -4.676/0.0269 ≈ -174. That matches the reported -175.5 in size and sign.

description: Moves the head weight out of Nesterov SGD into its own Muon instance (lr HEAD_LR, linear decay applied as before), with Muon's filter check extended to accept 2D tensors.
Raise the training translation pad from 2 to 4 pixels (reflect pad, random crop back to 32x32) to test stronger shift augmentation, leaving the predict-time TTA unchanged.

After training, recompute every BatchNorm's running statistics from 10,000 clean, un-augmented normalized training images in batches of 2000 (cumulative average), then restore momentum and switch to eval, so the statistics match the unaugmented test distribution.
Floor the linear LR decay at 10% of its initial value by changing both schedule factors to 1 - 0.9*step*base, leaving the Muon target-magnitude schedule and all base step counts unchanged.

Average the softmax probabilities of the TTA views instead of their raw logits in _get_tta_logits, then take the log so the output stays logit-like; uncertainty selection and view construction are unchanged.
Draws the brightness shift and contrast scale independently per colour channel, shape (B, 3, 1, 1), instead of once per image, keeping the same ranges, enable flag and compute cost.
Replace the fixed head output scale 1/x.size(-1) with a learnable scalar nn.Parameter initialised to 1/256 (reset in reset()) and trained in its own no-weight-decay SGD group at HEAD_LR.
Replace the BatchNorm epsilon of 1e-12, which rounds to zero in half precision and lets near-constant channels divide by zero and produce NaN/inf logits, with the standard 1e-5.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff changes one line inside the Muon optimizer step: norm_freq goes from the schedule 2 + int(15 * progress) to a constant 1. Nothing is carried between runs, nothing is seeded, the test images are not used for training, and no files are accessed.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. This is a real optimizer setting, and normalising on every step only adds compute. The variable `progress` is now unused in this function. That is harmless, but it can be removed to keep the code clean.
The numbers fit the reject decision. The candidate scores +0.0123, which is worse, and comes from a single run. A single job has noise sd of about 0.026, so the gap is well within noise.

My recomputed z is -0.458, using 0.0123 / (0.026 * sqrt(1 + 1/15)). This leaves out any 'worse' sign convention. The harness reports -0.463. The small difference probably comes from a slightly different sd estimate and does not change the decision.

description: Set the Muon gradient-norm rescaling to run every step by fixing norm_freq at 1 in Muon.step, leaving the rest of the update unchanged.
Dynamic pruning of the 25% lowest-loss samples in the second half of training, with per-sample running losses and step count recomputed from the kept set.
Replace the every-other-epoch whole-dataset flip with an independent per-sample horizontal flip applied to each training batch inside the loader, removing the pre-flipped cache.

Progressive resolution: for the first 40% of steps, bilinear-antialias downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 and compile the training step statically (dynamic=False), with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so both resolutions feed the head 256 features.

issues: No measurement workaround found: the low-resolution phase (first 40% of steps at 24x24) is computed inside train() on every run, there is no seeding and no file access, and test images are not used. predict() is unchanged and runs at full resolution.

AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) gives the same output as MaxPool2d(3) on the 3x3 map produced at 32x32, so inference is unchanged. At 24x24 the map is 2x2, where a fixed 3x3 pool would have failed, so the change is needed.

With dynamic=False there are two input shapes and so two compiles. Both should be triggered in the untimed first call, which runs the same schedule, so timed runs should not pay for compiling. Worth confirming that the median time does not include a recompile.
The whitening filters are set from 32x32 patch statistics but are applied to downscaled inputs early in training. This is a quality question, not a bug.

Only 2 candidate runs, and they differ by 0.057 (about 2.2 job sds), which is a somewhat wide spread. Recomputed z with the stated sd of 0.026 is about 7.90, consistent with the harness's 7.966. The decision to accept is robust.

description: Progressive resolution: for the first 40% of steps, bilinear-antialias downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 and compile the training step statically (dynamic=False), with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so both resolutions feed the head 256 features.

Removes the whitening bias from the Nesterov SGD param groups and forces whiten_bias_grad=False so the bias is frozen (and the LR schedule indices are remapped so the norm-bias and head groups keep their existing decay); note the bias is frozen at its random reset value, not zero, since reset() re-initialises it.
